title: Linux 6.11 on the ESP32-S3
note: Linux-on-esp32-S3 by svermigo (GPL-3.0): the esp-hosted network adapter on core 0, Linux executing in place from flash on core 1, cramfs root, jffs2 /etc and /home. Log in as root, password changeme123 — click the console and type; bash, MicroPython and fork are all there

title: …logged in for you
note: same image, a script types the login at 24 s and runs uname -a

title: …in a full terminal (xterm.js)
note: same image, logged in by the script, on a VT100 terminal: colours, cursor movement, line editing and full-screen programs render properly — try `ls --color`, `top`, `vi`, or `micropython`

title: IDF hello_world
note: boots the ROM, prints, reboots through the watchdog

title: Touch-LCD-4B energy panel
note: LVGL 480x480 over the RGB bus, GT911 touch — swipe between pages; demo data from energydata.json, tiles toggle; the SID player is on the last page (enable audio)

title: …with the SID player playing
note: same firmware, a script swipes to the SID page and presses play at 5.5 s

title: Pocket Tank · an LLM aquarium
note: mediacutlet/pocket-tank (MIT) on the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.8: a 14.3M-parameter 4-bit transformer decides what each fish does, running from flash on PIE (the S3's SIMD) while the other core renders the tank. Tap or drag to touch; type director commands such as feed 6 or shadow in the line box (help lists them). Slower than real time in the browser

title: ESP32-C3 · hello_world (RISC-V)
note: the other chip: one RV32IMC core, console only — real mask ROM through the bootloader into FreeRTOS. Verified line-for-line against a physical C3.

title: ESP32-C6 · hello_world (RISC-V)
note: the newest chip: one RV32IMAC core, console only — real mask ROM through the bootloader into FreeRTOS. Verified line-for-line against a Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47.

title: ESP32-C6 · 802.15.4 energy scanner
note: the Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47: LVGL spectrum of channels 11–26 on the ST7789 over SPI2 and DMA, the WS2812 blinking per scan, energy detect from the emulated 802.15.4 MAC with a moving 2.4 GHz picture — press BOOT for single-channel mode

title: ESP32-C6 · Contiki-NG
note: Contiki-NG on the ESP32-C6 as an unmodified IDF app: its own scheduler, CSMA and 802.15.4 stack over the emulated MAC, broadcasting every 5 s and blinking the WS2812 through the RMT

title: …two of them on one radio medium
note: two emulated C6 motes on one 802.15.4 medium, in this tab, with no simulator behind them: each hears the other's broadcasts. The second powers on 1.3 s later — two identical images booted together stay deterministic to the cycle and every frame collides

title: …an RPL/IPv6 network: root and client
note: two emulated C6 motes in this tab: node 1 is Contiki-NG's rpl-udp server and the DAG root, node 2 the client — it joins the DAG, then sends a UDP request every 10 s and gets a reply. 6LoWPAN, RPL Lite and CSMA end to end over the emulated 802.15.4 MAC, hardware ACKs included

title: ESP32-P4 + ESP32-C6 · WiFi through a co-processor
note: two chips in this tab, as on the Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6: the P4 (rev ≥ 3, two RISC-V cores) runs IDF's wifi_station with ESP-Hosted, the C6 the ESP-Hosted slave, both from their mask ROMs and in lock-step over SDIO. The C6 joins the virtual access point and the P4 gets its address through it. A real board with a v3.2 P4 and its own C6 goes through the same steps to its address

title: ESP32-P4 · Scintilla synth (Touch-LCD-3.5)
note: the Elka Synthex in integer C on the Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-3.5: LVGL on the ST7796 over SPI and DMA, FT5x06 touch, the ES8311's audio — enable audio and play the keys; tap the red display for the 80 presets, INSTRUMENT edits the sound live. Slower than real time in the browser

title: Schematik T-Display · classic ESP32 (Arduino)
note: a restyled Schematik Arduino sketch on the classic ESP32: a lowercase wordmark, four fun lines and verified emulator specs on the ST7789. GPIO35 advances; GPIO0 powers off into deep sleep and wakes back to the wordmark. No physical-board verification

title: LilyGO TTGO T-Display · spot prices (MicroPython)
note: the classic ESP32: stock MicroPython v1.29.0 (ESP32_GENERIC) from micropython.org, booted by the mask ROM, running a pure-Python spot-price app on its ST7789 135×240 over VSPI from a LittleFS filesystem — day prices as a bar chart with the current hour. Demo data from its own filesystem: the browser has no sockets, so there is no Wi-Fi and no fetch; the two buttons are below the panel

title: Atech 14-port Pocket Synth
note: Arduino firmware on the 14-port board: ST7735 display, WS2812 ring, encoder and buttons, SID-chip synth — the script plays it (enable audio)

title: …as a C64 SID jukebox
note: same firmware: cRSID emulates a whole C64 — 6502, SID, CIA, VIC — so it plays real .sid tunes. Commando by Rob Hubbard, then Wizball (enable audio)
